subject: Glimmer users: Better error logging now available

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Glimmer users: Better error logging now available
parts:
Good news for Glimmer users! Up until now, when a hosted Shiny application exits you generally had no way to see what went wrong. We've recently added better error logging that should make it much easier to diagnose such problems.
  • If the R process is not able to start, an error log is displayed directly in the web browser, if applicable. Example

  • Some of you have experienced the "RWebsocket closed unexpectedly" which really means "the app was able to get started but then exited with an error". I changed the wording to be more friendly, and the contents of the log file are now dumped to the JavaScript console. See here to learn how to open the JS console in various browsers. You can try it yourself with this example.

  • A unique error log file is created in the ~/ShinyApp/log directory each time one of your applications is started by Shiny. You can access this directory using RStudio Server's Files tab or using ssh. These log files are deleted automatically when the process exits, unless the process terminated abnormally (non-zero return code) or at an unexpected time. So if you start to see your ~/ShinyApp/log directory filling up with log files then you know your application is crashing all the time.
Hope that you find this functionality helpful!
